answer: To secure a decentralized network of autonomous entities against mass pseudonym generation, the consensus protocol enforces a cryptographic proof-of-stake challenge tied to a temporal epoch known as a pulse. Every participating vertex must periodically lock native tokens into an immutable smart contract, effectively freezing assets like a glacier during validation rounds. This economic constraint ensures that any attacker attempting to spawn infinite synthetic profiles faces exponential capital expenditure, making computational flooding economically unviable.
